category_title: Students with severe disabilities who use shouting and aggression to communicate basic needs
minimal_context: The student is participating in an interactive gaming activity during school time, where the goal is to imitate the adult using building blocks.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's play with the building blocks. Watch me put this block on top, and then you copy what I do.

STUDENT: (Looks at the blocks with a poor, stereotypical range of emotional expression, unable to execute the simple task of imitating the action.)

TUTOR: Come on, it's your turn. Pick up the block and put it here.

STUDENT: (Shows severely impaired nonverbal communication, making no attempt to interact with the blocks, but displays a predominant, stereotypical smile.)

TUTOR: Since you aren't doing it, I am going to take these blocks away and we are going to change to a different game right now.

STUDENT: (Reacts to the sudden environmental change and stress by bursting into loud laughter as a defense mechanism, displaying tension in this inappropriate situation.)

options.A: Place a sticker on the building block to show the student which part to touch.
options.B: Support verbal language with gestures and specific tonality during the building block activity.
options.C: Provide positive attention when the student displays positive behavior, and ignore harmless negative behaviors.
options.D: Provide a visual chart with names and times, and announce the game's duration beforehand.
